title: Ford Mustang GT RTR Spec 3: 2025

scenes.headline: Front Fascia
scenes.narration: The Ford Mustang GT RTR Spec 3, with its striking angular headlights and split grille, is all about a race-ready look.

scenes.headline: Rear Spoiler
scenes.narration: That rear spoiler not only enhances the aggressive stance but also contributes crucially to its aerodynamic efficiency.

scenes.headline: Tri-bar Taillights
scenes.narration: The distinctive tri-bar taillight design, paired with the color-shift wrap, makes the Mustang stand out even from behind.

scenes.headline: Performance Supercharger
scenes.narration: Under the hood, a Whipple supercharger pushes the 5.0-liter V8 to deliver 750 horsepower and 670 lb-ft of torque.

scenes.headline: High-Tech Cabin
scenes.narration: Inside, dual infotainment screens and a digital cluster modernize the feel, complemented by contrast stitching on the leather seats.
The RTR grille with its horizontal splitter isn't just for looks; it improves air intake efficiency.

scenes.headline: Beam vs. Camaro
scenes.narration: Compared to the Camaro SS which boasts 455 hp, the Mustang's 750 hp shows its track-ready potential.

scenes.headline: Limited Edition
scenes.narration: Each Mustang GT RTR Spec 3 is uniquely numbered, like 0161, underscoring its exclusivity.
With prices starting around $75,000, it's not cheap, but it offers significant value for performance enthusiasts.
So, does the RTR Spec 3's power make it your dream Mustang? Let us know in the comments.

script: The Ford Mustang GT RTR Spec 3, with its striking angular headlights and split grille, is all about a race-ready look. That rear spoiler not only enhances the aggressive stance but also contributes crucially to its aerodynamic efficiency. The distinctive tri-bar taillight design, paired with the color-shift wrap, makes the Mustang stand out even from behind. Under the hood, a Whipple supercharger pushes the 5.0-liter V8 to deliver 750 horsepower and 670 lb-ft of torque. Inside, dual infotainment screens and a digital cluster modernize the feel, complemented by contrast stitching on the leather seats. The RTR grille with its horizontal splitter isn't just for looks; it improves air intake efficiency. Compared to the Camaro SS which boasts 455 hp, the Mustang's 750 hp shows its track-ready potential. Each Mustang GT RTR Spec 3 is uniquely numbered, like 0161, underscoring its exclusivity. With prices starting around $75,000, it's not cheap, but it offers significant value for performance enthusiasts. So, does the RTR Spec 3's power make it your dream Mustang? Let us know in the comments.
